root_causes.description: The product-catalog service exhibits saturated server-side latency: p99 (and p50/p95/max) response time is pinned at 10000 ms, the histogram ceiling, throughout the incident window. Error rate, CPU, memory and restart count are all normal, isolating a pure latency injection in product-catalog, which is a leaf dependency of frontend, checkout and recommendation.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 latency < 100 ms (server-side histogram quantile, normal operating range)

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 (no server errors) for entire window
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01 — confirms latency fault, not an error/abort fault
no CPU saturation — rules out cpu_stress
no memory growth — rules out memory_stress

root_causes.description: frontend is a direct caller of product-catalog (frontend → product-catalog) and would inherit the 10 s tail latency on catalog-dependent requests. Plausible downstream-impact candidate, but the primary fault originates in the product-catalog leaf.

evidence.observed_value: product-catalog p99=10000 ms propagated over frontend → product-catalog dependency edge (from get_service_topology)
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 stable when product-catalog p99 < 100 ms

root_causes.description: checkout depends on product-catalog (checkout → product-catalog) and could show elevated end-to-end latency as a downstream consequence. This is impact, not an independent root cause.

evidence.observed_value: product-catalog p99=10000 ms, a shared dependency of checkout per service topology
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout p99 stable when product-catalog is healthy

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog service internals for an injected latency fault (e.g. artificial sleep/delay flag in flagd) and clear the 'product-catalog-high_latency-seed42' fault flag.
Roll/restart the product-catalog deployment to shed any wedged state causing the 10 s server-side stalls, then confirm p99 returns to < 100 ms.
Verify recovery up the dependency chain: frontend, checkout and recommendation p99 latency should normalize once product-catalog is fast.
Add a p99 latency alert on product-catalog server spans (threshold ~500 ms) to catch tail-latency injection earlier than error-rate alerts, since this fault produced zero errors.
